Refine the do not count/print generic flash chip entries conditions Corresponds to r1488 from upstream. Commit log from upstream: Previously only the generic "unknown XXXX SPI chips" were ignored (because their name started with "unknown". This patch adds also all chips whose vendor starts with "Unknown" (none so far) and "Programmer" (currently used by the opaque flash chip framework) . A patch will add the SFDP chip template with an "Unknown" vendor field later. Rationale: these entries do not contain any useful information when shown in -L or wiki output. It would be better to add them to a general feature section or similar. libcontainer: Separate cgroup configuration from creation This adds the ability to set the owner of the parent cgroups, this is needed when entering a cgroup namespace as the subdirectories and their files must be owned by the user that root maps to outside the container. Move cgroup creation from where the config is created until later. This information isn't known by login manager when creating the container. Moving it later allows it to be configured like other config options. BUG=none TEST=run with dependent changes and see that the cgroup is created with the correct owner and at the correct place in the cgroup hierarchy. Change-Id: Ia31fb7eebe562b36216ce547c9889bcffba7f257 Signed-off-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/362097 Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org>

login: Set cgroup parent directory for android containers Android will now run in a new cgroup namespace. This will allow it to modify its own cgroups while not knowing that it is part of a larger cgroup hierarchy. Configure the external cgroup "session_manager_containers" that will be the root of Android's cgroup namespace. BUG=b/29259708 TEST=Start android and check that it is in a new cgroup namespace rooted at session_manager_containers. Change-Id: Ic361c2cf0904d05b959fad51c53b2fd983b22bc9 Signed-off-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/362099 Reviewed-by: Dan Erat (OOO 8-12 to 8-22) <derat@chromium.org>

libcontainer: Run containers in a cgroup namespace Now that all of our supported kernels support cgroup namespaces, enable them when running a container. This will allow the container to modify cgroup parameters for sub groups but still allows the system to control overall limits. The contained processes will not know that it is in a cgroup namespace, it appears as the root inside the namespace. BUG=b/29259708 TEST=boot android on cyan and check cgroup membership inside and outside the container. Change-Id: I83e93ea6135f2b3f4baa4816eacacd1e02f1986a Signed-off-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/362350

g: implement firmware upgrade protocol version 3 This patch modifies CR50 code to switch to firmware update protocol version 3. In this version both SPI and USB updates use exactly the same messages (apart from the size field added by USB to help reassembly of the fragmented frames). Bot unused RO and RW sections can be now programmed. BRANCH=none BUG=chrome-os-partner:55789 TEST=on a Kevin running the existing cr50 image programmed the new cr50 image, restarted the device, programmed the cr50 image again (this time using version 3), restarted the device, then programmed both RO and RW images and restarted the device. Each time verified that the proper image is running. Introduce protected member for Service auto connect cooldown max Commit 0801d19 ("Throttle AutoConnect calls") introduces a cooldown timeout max of 30 minutes for all services in order to avoid a busy cycle that occurs on cellular devices when Service::Connect fails. This poses a problem for jetstream routers that are unable to acquire dhcp leases due to a downed ISP server as they become defunct for 30 minutes and require a power cycle. This change modifies the default timeout for all services to be 1 minute and introduces a protected member, max_auto_connect_cooldown_time_milliseconds_, which is overridden to be the previous 30 minute value for cellular services only. BUG=b:27207845 TEST=Added log to Service::ThrottleFutureAutoConnects and verified that net.log shows values reaching up to 1 minute on veyron_minnie-cheets. To test the cellular case, added conditional log to Service::ThrottleFutureAutoConnects and verified that max cooldown is set to the original 30 minutes on a link. Change-Id: I142951a12ab00e8a963a60adda98d5e125f3f78b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/367500 Commit-Ready: Ian Wyszynski <wyszynski@google.com> Tested-by: Ian Wyszynski <wyszynski@google.com> Reviewed-by: Ian Wyszynski <wyszynski@google.com> Reviewed-by: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org>
